name: Schizencephaly

criteria.description: Presence of a full-thickness cleft lined by gray matter extending from the ependymal surface of the lateral ventricle to the pial surface of the cerebral cortex
Cleft walls lined by heterotopic or dysplastic gray matter
Communication of the cleft with the lateral ventricle
Presence of associated brain malformations such as polymicrogyria or agenesis of the septum pellucidum

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Identification of a full-thickness cleft lined by gray matter extending from the lateral ventricle to the cortical surface on neuroimaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: MRI is the preferred imaging modality to confirm diagnosis

imaging: MRI demonstrating full-thickness cleft lined by gray matter extending from lateral ventricle to cortex
genetic: Mutations in EMX2 gene reported in some familial cases
Mostly sporadic with unclear genetic etiology
other: Prenatal ultrasound may detect large clefts or ventriculomegaly
EEG abnormalities consistent with epileptiform activity

distinguishingFeatures: Porencephalic cysts lack gray matter lining
Usually acquired postnatally due to ischemic or hemorrhagic injury
Polymicrogyria involves abnormal cortical layering without full-thickness clefts

redFlags: Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as vomiting and bulging fontanelle
references: Barkovich AJ, et al. Pediatric Neuroimaging. 5th ed. 2012.
Guerrini R, Dobyns WB. Malformations of cortical development: clinical features and genetic causes. Lancet Neurol. 2014.
